finding.title: Add per-row exception isolation to every EntityMerger except LearnerProfileMerger
finding.why: LearnerProfileMerger wraps each row's merge body in try/catch with an explicit rationale (learner_profile_merger.dart:35-37): 'a single malformed/FK-violating profile row must never abort the whole page... The per-row merger try/catch is the primary guard' — a claim echoed verbatim at the sync_orchestrator.dart call site. None of the other 16 merge implementations apply that pattern: any exception thrown while processing row 5 of a 200-row page (an FK violation — see the companion finding on stage_definition/settings/goal — or any malformed-field cast) propagates out of merge() and aborts the whole page. sync_orchestrator.dart's outer per-step catch keeps the app from crashing (it logs 'sync_pull_step_db_error_nonfatal' and returns), but the other 199 rows in that page are silently deferred to the next full sync instead of 199/200 succeeding immediately.
finding.recommendation: Generalize LearnerProfileMerger's per-row try/catch (log via AppLogger, continue to the next row) to the other 16 EntityMerger implementations, or centralize the isolation once inside MergeRouter.dispatch if it's restructured to iterate rows itself.
acceptance_criteria: A fault-injection test (parametrized over EntityKind.all where practical) merges a page containing one deliberately-malformed/throwing row alongside a valid row and asserts the valid row still applies and the bad one is logged, not that the whole page is dropped.

finding.title: Split the four hand-written files in core/sync/merge that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.rule: AG-3 (hand-written Dart file <=400 lines; generated exempt)
finding.why: drift_merge_store.dart alone blends the LWW clock-skew gate, seven distinct per-entity upsert implementations, FK/account resolution logic and schedule JSON encoding in one file — the 'God File' shape AG-3's cap exists to prevent — and it is this batch's #1 churn hotspot, so every fix wave re-reads all 788 lines for context. The three oversized test files mirror the same sprawl.
finding.recommendation: Split drift_merge_store.dart into one file per upsert group behind the existing MergeStore interface; split drift_merge_store_test.dart/mergers_test.dart/notification_settings_merger_round_trip_test.dart to mirror, no behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: AG-3 line-count checker (grep/lint over lib/ and test/, generated files exempt) passes for all four files.

finding.title: Remove or reconcile the dead LWW/merge-forward helpers in merge_rules.dart
finding.rule: Dead code / Fowler speculative generality; Evans ubiquitous-language drift (file claims authority it no longer has)
finding.why: A repo-wide grep shows lwwMerge, mergeForwardMaxInt, mergeForwardMaxDate, mergeForwardUnion and MergeResult are referenced only by test/features/sync/domain/merge_rules_test.dart and one story-acceptance test — no production merger calls any of them; the real LWW gate is DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer. The file's doc comment ('Conflict resolution rules for non-event-log data... These rules handle the rest') presents itself as the authoritative merge-rule library, misleading a reader when 12 of 13 LWW mergers actually moved to DriftMergeStore in the documented 'Phase 3' upgrade.
finding.recommendation: Once StudyDayConfigMerger is migrated off this file's remoteIsNewer (see the paired finding), delete the unused functions/class and their now-orphaned tests, or correct the file's doc comment to state it is superseded/test-only.
acceptance_criteria: Post-fix grep confirms merge_rules.dart has zero production callers left; file is either deleted or its doc comment is corrected.

finding.title: Extract the duplicated learnerProfiles FK-guard full-table-scan shared by three append-only mergers
finding.why: The identical 3-line 'load every learner_profiles row into a Set to guard an FK' snippet is copy-pasted across three mergers, each re-running the full scan once per merge() call. Harmless at today's family-sized profile counts, but three independent copies will silently diverge if the guard logic ever needs to change (e.g. excluding soft-deleted profiles).
finding.recommendation: Extract a shared `Future<Set<int>> existingProfileIds()` helper (on UserDatabase or a small mixin) and call it from all three mergers.
acceptance_criteria: One shared helper exists with its own unit test; the three call sites use it with no behavior change (existing points_sync_merger_test.dart and learning_ledger_merger_test.dart continue to pass).

finding.title: Fix hand-rolled test _FakeMergeStore.remoteIsNewer implementations to match DriftMergeStore's clock-skew/D15 semantics

evidence.quote:
// Mirror DriftMergeStore semantics: strict `remote > local` outside
    // the ±5 s window; inside the window, server timestamp decides.

finding.why: mergers_test.dart's fake claims to 'Mirror DriftMergeStore semantics' but omits the D15 fallback (drift_merge_store.dart:140-146): inside the clock-skew window with no decisive synced_at on both sides, the fake unconditionally prefers remote, whereas the real store first falls back to comparing raw updated_at (protecting a newer un-pushed local edit from being clobbered by an older remote). notification_settings_merger_round_trip_test.dart's fake is simpler still — no clock-skew window at all. Neither test currently uses timestamps close enough to trigger the divergent branch, so the suite passes today, but any future near-tie/clock-skew test added against these fakes would silently validate the WRONG (pre-D15) behavior, hiding exactly the bug class DriftMergeStoreTest exists to pin down.
finding.recommendation: Replace both hand-rolled remoteIsNewer bodies with a delegate to the real DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer (construct a throwaway DriftMergeStore over an in-memory DB inside the fake, or extract the pure comparison so both share one implementation) instead of re-deriving the algorithm by hand.
acceptance_criteria: A within-skew-window / no-syncedAt / older-remote test case added to either file fails before the fix and passes after, or the fake is proven identical to DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer by delegation (making such drift structurally impossible).
